steps.text: Rhodes Island Landship
'Lutra Workshop'

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Don't blink now, Closure.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Meeboo SUPER, select M-11 Originium-Proof Coating from the table.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: (There's a dozen types of coating here, and they all pretty much look and feel the same sans packaging.)

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Got it in one.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: C'mon, that's just basic stuff.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: There's a broken component in this thermal sensor. Repair it in three minutes, Meeboo SUPER.

steps.name: Meeboo SUPER
steps.text: Repair complete. There is an electronic component under the base that compromises thermal sensor efficiency. It has been removed without affecting device operation.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Sweet! Took less than two!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Wow! It talks!

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: What's a smart upgrade without a voice module?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Took some time to get used to it myself. It's not exactly the chatty type, though.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Did you really have to make the voice so gruff though...? Whatever, to each their own.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Keep going.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Meeboo SUPER, set a new password for the workshop door.

steps.name: Meeboo SUPER
steps.text: Password set using a combination of alphanumeric characters in upper and lower cases, and special characters. Password does not include your birthday.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Alright, awesome!

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Applied testing, phase one complete!

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: And there you have it, the new, the improved, the Meeboo SUPER! So? What'd ya think? Smarter than your AI buggies, right?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Sure is a clever little guy! But Lancet-2 or Castle-3 could do all that, no problem.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hey, no biting! You're just like Mayer!

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Let her go for now, Meeboo SUPER.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Can't tell if its performance is better than the buggies, but it sure holds a grudge better.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Stay away!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: So, how much time did this upgrade take you?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Lemme see... three months, ish?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Closure, Closure! I've got that 'Raythean Challenger Hellcat Demon High-Performance Operation Platform' upgrade proposal you wanted!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Thanks. Next up is—

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Nah, I need a month off.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Whoa, a workaholic like you? Burnt out? Or... are you looking for a raise?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: No way, you know me.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Just finished up all my requests from Rhine Lab and Rhodes Island, so my schedule's a clear blue sky.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: And it's high time I upgraded the Meeboos.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Haven't you been doing that in your spare time? What do you need more time for all of a sudden?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Three more Meeboos have gone kaput the last few months, and there's still a whole pile waiting for repair.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: There's only one 1st-gen left.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Aw, poor little guys.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Their efficiency's improved, but survival rate remains poor in adverse environments, or operations requiring a high degree of precision.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Implementing a full AI should let 'em properly take care of themselves while performing their tasks.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Oh, I'll help then!

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Thanks, but no thanks. I'll be fine on my own.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Why not? Didn't we work together on Iwona's Justice Knight?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: That was a PRTS-based customization. Not even you know the ins and outs of the buggies' operational algorithms.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: That's not what I want for my babies. From Rhine to Rhodes, I've always worked on 'em myself.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I'll give you a shout if I've got any questions, though.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I'd installed a learning system on 'em, but that's not even in the same ballpark as true 'intelligence.' Needed to start from scratch.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: First I tried optimizing the existing Meeboo core to improve its automation logic, but the results weren't too great.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: So I rewrote the underlying code... Which took a while.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Original plan called for five SUPER prototypes to get some proper control experiments in, but I only managed to finish one.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Still! This Meeboo SUPER is an unprecedented achievement with applications in highly complex environments, including demolition, surveying, reconnaissance, combat, and everyday life.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Most importantly, it can complete precise operations fully independently.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: It'll be the most powerful smart machine in all Terra... Small and easy to mass produce too. Makes your customized buggies look like a science fair project.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: We're talking about a whole Meeboo army!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: So what's this tag on it?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Nametag. Got one on every Meeboo.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But why so many? Let's see, C00-1, B03-4, B12, G70...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Took 'em off of decommissioned Meeboos.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Yeah, I know, but weren't those supposed to go in the Great Meeboos Monument? Did you...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: So the Meeboo SUPER carries on its brothers' hopes and dreams?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Hehe.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But you still left yourself control permissions for the Meeboo's core, yeah?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I guess.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Then it's not quite 'smart' enough, yet.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I'll start the next phase of applied testing in a couple days.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I'll see you then, then.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: By the way, make sure you've got the settings right on the Meeboo SUPER's demolition program. We are on the landship, after all...

spans.text: By the way, make sure you've got the settings right on the Meeboo SUPER's demolition program. We

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Now I just gotta log today's test data.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hey, are you even listening, Mayer?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I know, I know.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Oh, right, what's the new door password, Meeboo SUPER?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Huh... Is that a bug?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Meeboo SUPER!

a.text: Meeboo SUPER Test Logs 07
Continuing applied testing for the Meeboo SUPER prototype today.
I'll temporarily disable my control permissions for the Meeboo core, allowing the Meeboo SUPER to autonomously inspect nearby buildings and resolve potential problems.
This is the most important stage.
Meeboo has learned to speak, though we're both still getting used to it. It's learning to complete more complex tasks; it's no longer just a 'walking bomb.'
However, this is the first time ever that a Meeboo will be operating outside my control.

If successful, it will mean that the Meeboos have truly reached the stage of artificial intelligence, without relying on the Rhodes Island mainframe, which is very important for both Lutra Workshop and the Meeboos.
Although there have been some occasional data deviations, based on the Meeboo SUPER's performance to date, I think there's a lot to look forward to in today's testing.
After all, every last Meeboo is lending us their strength.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Core control permission off.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Meeboo SUPER, scan and resolve potential issues for buildings in the designated area.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Of course, since we're on the Rhodes Island Landship, you'll need to...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Oh, what am I saying, you're smart, you know what to do, right? Haha.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Whew—

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Now just gotta wait for it to finish the job and come back.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Wow, the requests sure have piled up... Guess I really put 'em off for too long.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Let's see... wall projectors for operator quarters, weapons system upgrade for the training grounds, synchronization between drones and charging equipment...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: And the workshop's a mess.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Might as well clean up the operating console while I have time.

steps.name: Meeboo SUPER
steps.text: Meeboo— SUPER. Scanning building. Resolving potential problems. Scanning building. Resolving potential problems.

steps.name: Meeboo SUPER
steps.text: 8 structural integrity issues found. Calculating. Issues resolved using method—

steps.name: Meeboo SUPER
steps.text: One remaining structure to inspect.
'Lutra Workshop'

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: There, that's more like it!

steps.name: Meeboo SUPER
steps.text: Full-area scan.

steps.name: Meeboo SUPER
steps.text: Retrieving comparison data. Activating analysis.

steps.name: Meeboo SUPER
steps.text: Results—

steps.name: Meeboo SUPER
steps.text: Area is larger than expected. Lacks distinction between living and working space. Presence of dangerous equipment—

steps.name: Meeboo SUPER
steps.text: Warning. Resolving potential issue. Evacuate area.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Now lemme fix these heat sensors.

steps.name: Meeboo SUPER
steps.text: Warning. Resolving potential issue. Evacuate area.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Running short on materials. Guess I'll need to submit another order to the Procurement Department...

steps.name: Meeboo SUPER
steps.text: Resolving issue using method— method—

steps.name: Meeboo SUPER
steps.text: Demolition.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Did something just move?
Mayer was not slow on the uptake, but she could have been faster if she had shaken the habit of working with her headphones on.
The Meeboo SUPER activates its detonation sequence.
Using an extendable robotic arm, Mayer manages to press the shock shield activation button just in time, deflecting the Meeboo SUPER's directional explosion.
Lutra Workshop's key areas were undamaged, but the extendable platform near the door holding heavy materials is destroyed.
Mayer watches as the Meeboo SUPER is buried in the rubble it created.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Argh!

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: So... heavy...! Good thing the robotic arm charging system still works.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Meeboo SUPER!
What's going on, Mayer? I could hear the noise from your workshop a mile away.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Whoa, the Meeboo SUPER... looks heavily damaged.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Did it do all this?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Can't say I blame it... I told you not to use your quarters as your workshop, and not to make unauthorized modifications. Lemme check if the load-bearing structure is still intact...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: What about the other places it inspected? Did it...?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I came from that way. Things look okay.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: (Good thing I set up those localized shock compensators ahead of time. Whew...)

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: How about you? You okay, Mayer?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Look at this mess. I'll help you clean up.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Just like the old days.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: The workshop's a mess... just like the old days.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Don't scare me like that! You hit your head or something? You're not the type to reminisce at the drop of a hat, are you?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I mean, back when I first started on the Meeboos...
Mayer's workshop again?
Third time this month, isn't it?
Chronometer stops working, cooling system malfunction... and now the chair springs up on its own and knocks the operating table over?
It's always one thing or another pulling her away from the project and back to her lab.
And all this after she was even given her own workshop...
If she says it's a coincidence, who are we to argue? Not worth wasting time worrying about.
I was so excited to get into Rhine Lab.
For researchers, it was the holy land for all of Columbia—all of Terra, even. It had the facilities, the projects, the talent, the pay, and the benefits.

We had a consensus that science would determine the future of Terra. Within Rhine Lab itself, however, everyone had their own interpretation of science, their own obsessions. Especially the directors.
It was an uncomfortable place. Some of the finest minds in the world, but woefully inefficient when they get together, like an all-star sports team that just can't seem to win.

I was in Engineering, providing technical support for the other sections. A project started by Energy last month, which was already halfway through preparations, was facing termination because of opposition from Control.
Similarly, the Defense Section could also put a stop to ongoing projects at their discretion.
This happened again and again at Rhine Lab. Low-level staff were in a constant cycle of installation, testing, and removal.
I felt like I was better off doing research on my own.

That's why I made a trick alarm clock that caused just a teensy bit of havoc in my workshop at preset times. Not enough to put the place out of commission, but serious enough that I'd have to rush back to deal with it.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: That was the first Meeboo prototype.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I gradually added more functions, and named them after the boot-up sound.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: So you'd run back to your lab, all excited to clean up the mess?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Yeah. Never made much progress on the projects they assigned me, but I sure invented plenty of little gizmos.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: After I helped her out, Silence liked some of the stuff I made and put in a recommendation. They still use 'em back at Rhine Lab, even.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The Meeboos were always the apple of your eye, though, weren't they?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Yeah, I wanted 'em to become these crazy smart machines.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I mean, they've been by my side this whole time, from Rhine to Rhodes.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: But after countless losses, decommissions, and upgrades... there was only one 1st-gen Meeboo left.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Meeboo SUPER...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Was built around the last 1st-gen, yeah.

a.text: Meeboo SUPER Test Logs 08
Internal sensor nodes malfunctioned. Major and irreversible warping of the limbs.
89.7% of the core is damaged. Repair would be difficult. There appear to be preexisting algorithmic issues, which had already manifested with the door password error.
Meeboo SUPER had worked independently for one hour prior to returning to Lutra Workshop, which was enough to overload its processing.
It saw items that operators left outside their doors as structural issues and blew them up...
That's not smart at all.
Sigh...
Analysis: The Meeboo SUPER prototype is no longer suited for practical operation.
Damage to the workshop's walls, loss of material... repairs will cost a fair bit.
Conclusion: This Meeboo upgrade is a failure.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hey, no one said artificial intelligence was easy.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Don't let it get to you!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Mayer!

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The Meeboo SUPER may not have achieved its goals, but it wasn't a complete failure.

spans.text: The Meeboo SUPER may not have achieved its goals, but it wasn't a

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: C'mon, we can all see what happened, Closure.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: No, I'm serious, look!

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: The nametags of the Meeboos.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Yeah. Its limbs are all crushed and warped, but the nametags have just fallen off, completely intact.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It's not like they're made of anything tougher than the main body, are they?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Wait, are you saying it...?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Could be a coincidence, or it could be some sort of 'instinct'...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Meeboo SUPER...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The voice module is too damaged to respond.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Beautiful! You should've seen the looks on their faces when I ditched.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: But I gotta scoot you over a little for next time. Knocking over a chair is one thing, but fixing broken equipment is a pain.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I should give you a name, huh... You know what, how about I set up a random boot-up sound for you? Whatever sound you make will be your new name!

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Over here, Meeboo. I need to reset the settings for your demolition program.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Meeboo, adjust the position of the robotic arm.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Meeboo, bring me that thermal device.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Meeboo... Hey, how'd you know I wanted this calibrator?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Whoa! What are you doing? Stop pulling!

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: It's just a bit of work. Not like I'm gonna forget to eat.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Er...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Fine, I get it, I'm eating, I'm eating!

a.text: Mayer picks up the name tags from the ground and wipes the dirt off them.
She does so carefully, like she is organizing experimental data or putting together a precision machine.
More carefully, in fact.
Mayer has developed many things: wire-controlled machines, energy coating, transmission systems... She has become numb to the joys of creation.
Is there surprise, excitement, pride? Yes.
But nothing too intense.
This is normal for a researcher. That is why she credits her achievements to the Lutra Workshop.
Even though she is the Lutra Workshop.
The Meeboos, however, were different.
She talked to them, worked with them, killed time with them, and brought them with her from Rhine Lab to Rhodes Island.
She asked them to respond, and they did.
Mayer gazes upon the remains of the Meeboo SUPER. It was, without a doubt, a failure, but Mayer feels something she had never felt before.
Sadness? Surprise? Joy? Yes.
But it is more than that. Stronger, more complex, harder to describe.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: So, not quite buggy tier yet, but Meeboo SUPER has made a lot of progress. Don't give up.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Can I get another two months off, then?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I want to start the next smart upgrade project based on these results! Strike while the iron is hot!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: No way, buster! I'm not falling for that!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I already gave you three months. Do you realize how many requests Engineering gets in three months?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: And you'll also need to submit a detailed report on what happened during the Meeboo SUPER's testing, especially the accident.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: And most importantly, you're paying for the Lutra Workshop's repairs out of your own pocket!
Meeboo SUPER Test Logs 09
This Meeboo upgrade has failed.
But the Meeboos are by Mayer's side. The possibilities are infinite.
Mayer trusts Meeboo.
Mayer trusts Mayer.
